question: Does a fixed rank-one rational-curve lift of every sampled subgroup point satisfy the L=4 bounded-coordinate premise?
field_rule: all eight selected fields in the pinned larger-order admission result
subgroup_generator: m times reduction of P, where m=ord(P mod p)/q and q is the selected prime subgroup order
query_law: complete t in [0,q) for each of the two independent offsets
lift_rule: for u=(17-t) mod q, centered(u)=u if u<=floor(q/2) else u-q; lift is m*centered(u)*P over Q
coordinate_radius_measure: maximum absolute rank-one coordinate for all two-point sums with coefficients in [-L,L]^2 and independent full t laws
claim_boundary: complete algebraic coordinate control; the lift rule uses subgroup scalar coordinates and is not an efficient ECDLP algorithm
